arxiv-2009-08840.title: Lightweight Detection of a Small Number of Large Errors in a Quantum Circuit
arxiv-2009-08840.creator: Noah Linden, Ronald de Wolf
arxiv-2009-08840.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Noah Linden, Ronald de Wolf. Suppose we want to implement a unitary U U , for instance a circuit for some quantum algorithm. Suppose our actual implementation is a unitary U ~ \tilde{U} , which we can only apply as a black-box. In general it is an exponentially-hard task to decide whether U ~ \tilde{U} equals the intended U U , or is significantly different in a worst-case norm.

arxiv-2102-05221.title: Early Abandoning and Pruning for Elastic Distances including Dynamic Time Warping Thanks: This research has been supported by Australian Research Council grant DP210100072.
arxiv-2102-05221.creator: Matthieu Herrmann, Geoffrey I. Webb
arxiv-2102-05221.description: Abstract Nearest neighbor search under elastic distances is a key tool for time series analysis, supporting many applications. However, straightforward implementations of distances require O ⁡ ( n 2 ) O(n^{2}) space and time complexities, preventing these applications from scaling to long series.

arxiv-2107-13876.title: Understanding the Effects of Adversarial Personalized Ranking Optimization Method on Recommendation Quality Conference: AdvML ’21: Workshop on Adversarial Learning Methods for Machine Learning and Data Mining; August 15, 2021; Singapore (virtual) AdvML ’21: Workshop on Adversarial Learning Methods f
arxiv-2107-13876.creator: Vito Walter Anelli, Yashar Deldjoo, Tommaso Di Noia, Felice Antonio Merra
arxiv-2107-13876.description: Abstract . Recommender systems (RSs) employ user-item feedback, e.g., ratings, to match customers to personalized lists of products. Approaches to top-k recommendation mainly rely on Learning-To-Rank algorithms and, among them, the most widely adopted is Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR), which bases on a pair-wise optimization approach. Recently, BPR has been found vulnerable against adversarial perturbations of its model parameters.

arxiv-2209-10230.title: Magic squares: Latin, Semiclassical and Quantum
arxiv-2209-10230.creator: Gemma De las Cuevas, Tim Netzer, Inga Valentiner-Branth
arxiv-2209-10230.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gemma De las Cuevas, Tim Netzer, Inga Valentiner-Branth. Quantum magic squares were recently introduced as a ‘magical’ combination of quantum measurements. In contrast to quantum measurements, they cannot be purified (i.e. dilated to a quantum permutation matrix)—only the so-called semiclassical ones can. Purifying establishes a relation to an ideal world of fundamental theoretical and practical importance; the opposite of purifying is described by the matrix convex hull.

arxiv-2305-03536.title: Shaping Next-Generation RAN Topologies to Meet Future Traffic Demands: A Peak Throughput Study
arxiv-2305-03536.creator: Paolo Fiore ∗ , Ilario Filippini ∗ and Danilo De Donno §
arxiv-2305-03536.description: Abstract Millimeter-Wave (mm-Wave) Radio Access Networks (RANs) are a promising solution to tackle the overcrowding of the sub-6 GHz spectrum, offering wider and underutilized bands. However, they are characterized by inherent technical challenges, such as a limited propagation range and blockage losses caused by obstacles.

arxiv-2312-09556.title: Optical Ranging Using Coherent Kerr Soliton Dual-microcombs with Extended Ambiguity Distance
arxiv-2312-09556.creator: Yuechen Yang 1, Yang Shen 1, Kailu Zhou 1, Chenhua Hu 2, Yuanzhuo Ding 1, Tinghao Jiang 1, Wei Li 3, Yudong Li 3, Liangsen Feng 3, Tengfei Wu 3, Guangqiang He 1,4
arxiv-2312-09556.description: Abstract Optical ranging is a key technology in metrology. Optical frequency combs are shown to provide several advantages in light ranging, offering high precision with high acquisition rate. However, performance of traditional ranging systems based on microcombs is limited by the short ambiguity distance and non-real-time processing.

arxiv-2404-01644.title: InsightLens : Augmenting LLM-Powered Data Analysis with Interactive Insight Management and Navigation
arxiv-2404-01644.creator: Luoxuan Weng, Xingbo Wang, Junyu Lu, Yingchaojie Feng, Yihan Liu, Haozhe Feng, Danqing Huang, and Wei Chen
arxiv-2404-01644.description: Abstract The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized the capabilities of natural language interfaces (NLIs) for data analysis. LLMs can perform multi-step and complex reasoning to generate data insights based on users’ analytic intents. However, these insights often entangle with an abundance of contexts in analytic conversations such as code, visualizations, and natural language explanations.

arxiv-2409-16762.title: Post- G ​ W GW theory and its application to pseudogap in strongly correlated system
arxiv-2409-16762.creator: Hui Li, Yingze Su, Junnian Xiong, Haiqing Lin, Huaqing Huang, Dingping Li
arxiv-2409-16762.description: Abstract The G ​ W GW approximation is a widely used framework for studying correlated materials, but it struggles with certain limitations, such as its inability to explain pseudogap phenomena. To overcome these problems, we propose a systematic theoretical framework for Green’s function corrections and apply it specifically to the G ​ W GW approximation.

arxiv-2505-21479.title: Are Language Models Consequentialist or Deontological Moral Reasoners?
arxiv-2505-21479.creator: Keenan Samway, Max Kleiman-Weiner, David Guzman Piedrahita, Rada Mihalcea, Bernhard Schölkopf, Zhijing Jin
arxiv-2505-21479.description: Abstract As AI systems increasingly navigate applications in healthcare, law, and governance, understanding how they handle ethically complex scenarios becomes critical. Previous work has mainly examined the moral judgments in large language models (LLMs), rather than their underlying moral reasoning process. In contrast, we focus on a large-scale analysis of the moral reasoning traces provided by LLMs.

arxiv-2510-25734.title: Ramsey Numbers in Kneser Graphs
arxiv-2510-25734.creator: Emily Heath, Grace McCourt, Alex Parker, Coy Schwieder, Shira Zerbib
arxiv-2510-25734.description: Abstract We define the r r -Kneser Ramsey number R r KG ​ ( s , t ) R^{\textrm{KG}}_{r}(s,t) as the minimum integer n n such that every red/blue edge-coloring of the Kneser graph KG ​ ( n , r ) \textrm{KG}(n,r) contains a red s s -clique or a blue t t -clique.

arxiv-2511-08598.title: OKBench: Democratizing LLM Evaluation with Fully Automated, On-Demand, Open Knowledge Benchmarking
arxiv-2511-08598.creator: Yanhong LiUniversity of Chicago yanhongli@uchicago.edu, Tianyang XuTTI-Chicago sallyxu@ttic.edu, Kenan TangUC Santa Barbara kenantang@ucsb.edu Karen LivescuTTI-Chicago klivescu@ttic.edu David McAllesterTTI-Chicago mcallester@ttic.edu Jiawei ZhouStony Brook University jiawei.zhou.1@stonybrook.edu
arxiv-2511-08598.description: Abstract Knowledge-intensive question answering is central to large language models (LLMs) and is typically assessed using static benchmarks derived from sources like Wikipedia and textbooks. However, these benchmarks fail to capture evolving knowledge in a dynamic world, and centralized curation struggles to keep pace with rapid LLM advancements.

arxiv-2604-11139.creator: Ioanna-Maria Lygatsika, Marc Sarraute, Lucas Baguet, Pierre Kestener, Marc Torrent

pmc-10661921.title: Applications of machine and deep learning to thyroid cytology and histopathology: a review
pmc-10661921.creator: Greg Slabaugh, Luis Beltran, Hasan Rizvi, Panos Deloukas, Eirini Marouli
pmc-10661921.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This review synthesises past research into how machine and deep learning can improve the cyto- and histopathology processing pipelines for thyroid cancer diagnosis. The current gold-standard preoperative technique of fine-needle aspiration cytology has high interobserver variability, often returns indeterminate samples and cannot reliably identify some pathologies; histopathology analysis addresses these issues to an extent, but it requires surgical resection of the suspicious lesions so cannot influence preoperative decisions.

pmc-11355199.title: Association between Atherogenic Dyslipidemia and Subclinical Myocardial Injury in the General Population
pmc-11355199.creator: Nada S. Elbadawi, Moaze H. Sobih, Mai Z. Soliman, Mohamed A. Mostafa, Richard Kazibwe, Elsayed Z. Soliman
pmc-11355199.description: Background: Subclinical myocardial injury (SCMI) is associated with an increased risk of poor cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes. Understanding the underlying risk factors for SCMI is crucial for the prevention and management of CVD. We hypothesized that atherogenic dyslipidemia, a combination of high triglycerides (TG) and low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), is associated with an increased risk of SCMI.

pmc-11401520.title: Sex Differences in the Associations Between Chronic Diseases and Insomnia Symptoms Among Older Adults in India
pmc-11401520.creator: T Muhammad, Milan Das, Arup Jana, Soomi Lee
pmc-11401520.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundSleep problems are a critical issue in the aging population, affecting quality of life, cognitive efficiency, and contributing to adverse health outcomes. The coexistence of multiple diseases is common among older adults, particularly women. This study examines the associations between specific chronic diseases, multimorbidity, and insomnia symptoms among older Indian men and women, with a focus on the interaction of sex in these associations.MethodsData were drawn from 31,464 individuals aged 60 and older in the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India, Wave-1 (2017–18).

pmc-12397389.title: Design and modeling of eye-shaped double-slot GaAs microring resonator for CO2 sensing
pmc-12397389.creator: Faezeh Pakfetrat, Mahdi Bahadoran, Shadab Dabagh, Francesco Chiavaioli
pmc-12397389.description: Monitoring of CO2 is crucial because of its profound impact on both environmental and human health. A novel highly sensitive refractive index (RI) sensor, utilizing a double-slot microring resonating structure, has been designed and numerically assessed for the sensitive detection of gas media.

pmc-12405798.title: Addressing Tobacco-Related Disparities Among Youth Experiencing Homelessness by Engaging Youth Collaborators in Intervention Research: Protocol for a Multimethod, Community-Based Participatory Research Study
pmc-12405798.creator: Alana R Lopez, Andrew C Lim, Renatta Escobedo, Nicole Chung, Lorilee Chien, Jerel P Calzo, Lianne Urada, Benjamín Aceves, Steven Jellá, Sabrina L Smiley, Jennifer K Felner
pmc-12405798.description: BackgroundYouth experiencing homelessness and housing instability exhibit disparities in tobacco use and co-use of tobacco and cannabis products compared to their stably housed peers. Interventions to address these disparities have had limited success to date. This may be related to a lack of fit between intervention approaches and the unique needs and preferences of this marginalized population.

pmc-12413454.title: Longitudinal associations between 24-hour movement behaviors and physical fitness in preschoolers: a compositional isotemporal substitution analysis
pmc-12413454.creator: Huiqi Song, Borui Zhang, Nike Lu, Yang Liu, Patrick W C Lau
pmc-12413454.description: This study investigated the prospective associations between changes in 24-h movement behaviors and physical fitness (PF) components in preschool children; and examined how the reallocation of time between movement behaviours was associated with longitudinal changes in PF. This is a two-year longitudinal study of 200 Chinese children aged 3–4 years old.

pmc-12457559.title: Citizen Science for Water Quality Monitoring: Analyzing Key Parameters, Success Factors, and Research Gaps for Aquaculture
pmc-12457559.creator: Walidatush Sholihah, Mohammad Gharesifard
pmc-12457559.description: Citizen science is often used as an approach for participatory water quality monitoring; however, its application in aquaculture remains limited. This study evaluates the current state of citizen science in monitoring water quality, with a particular focus on its implications for aquaculture practices.

pmc-12780042.title: Self-assembled cellulosic superstructures with unanticipated high quantum yields
pmc-12780042.creator: Cheng Li, Zhen Lang, Jade Poisson, Wenbo Chen, Caoxing Huang, Evgeny Nimerovsky, Philipp Vana, Kai Zhang
pmc-12780042.description: Nonconventional luminophores devoid of traditional, large π-conjugates often suffer from low solid-state fluorescence quantum yields (FLQYs). In parallel, self-assembled bowl-shaped and helical architectures at the micro- and macroscale are unusual (mostly reported at the nanoscale). Here, we report that surface-stearoylated cellulose nanocrystals and cellulose stearoyl esters co-assemble into macroscale helices (FLQY: 86%) with diameters of 32−104 μm.

pmc-12788451.title: Assessment of ECG Changes in Hypothyroid Patients and Their Correlation with Serum TSH Levels
pmc-12788451.creator: Mahi J. Khiloshiya, Tirth H. Vyas, Ashka Priyadarshi, Sanket R. Patel, Anuj S. Modi, Swati Mahajan
pmc-12788451.description: Background:Hypothyroidism, a common endocrine disorder, is known to influence cardiovascular physiology, particularly through its effects on cardiac electrophysiology. Electrocardiographic (ECG) abnormalities, such as bradycardia, low-voltage complexes, and prolonged QT intervals, are frequently observed. The relationship between the severity of hypothyroidism, often measured by serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, and the extent of ECG changes remains a subject of clinical relevance.

pmc-13181529.title: Physicochemical characterization of etch‐and‐rinse adhesive system doped with catechin‐loaded polymeric microparticles
pmc-13181529.creator: Jiovanne Rabelo Neri, Nadine Luisa Guimarães Albuquerque, Marcelo Victor Sidou Lemos, Monica Yamauti, Francisco Fábio Oliveira de Sousa, Vanara Florêncio Passos, Sérgio Lima Santiago
pmc-13181529.description: This study evaluated the incorporation of epigallocatechin‐3‐gallate (EGCG)‐loaded poly(lactide‐co‐glycolide) (PLGA) microparticles into a two‐step etch‐and‐rinse adhesive and their effects on physicochemical properties and EGCG release. EGCG was added to Single Bond 2 either directly (0.01% and 0.1% w/w) or encapsulated in PLGA 50:50 or 75:25 microparticles (0.5%–2% w/w). Cumulative release was measured by UV–Vis spectrophotometry.

pmc-13205371.title: Effects of Ultrasonic Scaling and Teeth Brushing on Surface Properties of PEEK Prosthetic Restorations
pmc-13205371.creator: Aleksandra D. Čairović, Mirjana M. Perić, Nevena Čairović, Luka Župac, Vesna M. Maksimović, Sanja S. Stevanović, Aleksandra B. Špadijer-Gostović, Dragan M. Stanimirović
pmc-13205371.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose: This study provides a comparative evaluation of surface changes in BioHPP materials under routine professional hygiene procedures, which is recommended by dentists, twice a year. BioHPP is a polyetheretherketone polymer used in prosthetic dentistry as a frame material. The aim was to investigate whether routine dental cleaning procedures such as ultrasonic scaling and brushing affect the surface proprieties of prosthetic BioHPP restorations.

pmc-13253978.title: Trapped Fourth Ventricle in a Pediatric Patient With a History of Post‐Traumatic Hydrocephalus and Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13253978.creator: Muhammad Hamza, Muhammad Ibrahim, Ihsan Ullah, Rehmat Farhaj, Fazeela Bibi, Khalil El Abdi, Bilal Aslam, Vohra Maham Hassan, Said Hamid Sadat

pmc-13272153.title: A prototype smartwatch for monitoring dynamic, compound and plyometric exercises in cancer prehabilitation: a development and validation study
pmc-13272153.creator: San San Tay, Hanushyah Devi, Shannon Yap, Abbas Bin Zainul Abideen, Xuan Han Koh, Daniel Leong
pmc-13272153.description: BackgroundCancer prehabilitation programmes increasingly rely on home-based exercise interventions, yet objective monitoring of exercise compliance remains challenging. Current commercial wearables focus primarily on aerobic activities and lack capability for monitoring dynamic, compound, and plyometric exercises essential for cancer prehabilitation.ObjectiveTo develop and validate a prototype smartwatch capable of monitoring specific prehabilitation exercises with objective compliance tracking.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3141.title: 18 U.S.C. § 3141 — Release and detention authority generally
uslaw-usc-t18-s3141.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s3141.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 207 (Release And Detention Pending Judicial Proceedings). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Pending Trial.— A judicial officer authorized to order the arrest of a person under section 3041 of this title before whom an arrested person is brought shall order that such person be released or detained.
